the infinite hill foundation

if you give inside infinite hill, we don't keep a cent of it.

the infinite hill foundation is a separate nonprofit (in formation — papers first, promises second). every donation made anywhere in infinite hill will go to it, and from there to the places it's meant for: the institutions our Keepers come from, scholarships so a kid or a family who can't pay gets the year anyway, and the free student and youth-group plans.

the company gives too

infinite hill is a company, on purpose. and part of what it earns goes to the foundation, not only what you give. once the paid plans open, we'll say exactly how much, and publish it every year.

0%, forever

infinite hill the company takes nothing from a gift. no fee, no "processing," no float. the foundation will have its own board and its own books, and we don't sit on the board alone. this isn't a marketing line — it's how the company is built, so it can't quietly change later.

every gift gives twice

planned — gifts aren't on sale during the pilot. when they are: buy someone a door — a hundred days, a year, a table — and a year also goes to someone who can't pay. we'll publish the count.

why a company at all, then?

because a business that funds its own mission never has to beg for it. the house is free forever and will stay free because plus and the table — planned, not on sale during the pilot — will pay for it. the foundation handles what should be given, and a share of what the company earns goes there too. sustainability is the moral position.

start now. it's free.
